question: Which statement about minimum spanning tree algorithms on a connected weighted undirected graph with V vertices and E edges is correct?
options: Kruskal's algorithm sorts the edges and uses a disjoint-set structure, running in O(E log E); Prim's algorithm with a binary heap runs in O(E log V).
Kruskal's algorithm grows a single tree from an arbitrary start vertex and runs in O(E + V log V) with a Fibonacci heap; Prim's algorithm sorts all edges first.
Prim's algorithm requires sorting all edges by weight and runs in O(E log E); Kruskal's algorithm runs in O(V²) with an adjacency matrix.
Both algorithms run in O(V²) with any graph representation; neither uses a priority queue or a disjoint-set structure.
gold_answer: Kruskal's algorithm sorts the edges and uses a disjoint-set structure, running in O(E log E); Prim's algorithm with a binary heap runs in O(E log V).
notes: All quoted passages were read live on 2026-11-19 from the two CC BY-SA 4.0 Wikipedia articles cited in the evidence. Running-time bounds are taken from the Kruskal Complexity section and the Prim Time complexity section; re-check those sentences before freezing.

positions.answer: Kruskal's algorithm grows a single tree from an arbitrary start vertex and runs in O(E + V log V) with a Fibonacci heap; Prim's algorithm sorts all edges first.

claims.text: Kruskal's algorithm sorts the edges by weight and uses a disjoint-set data structure to detect cycles.

evidence.text: It is a greedy algorithm that in each step adds to the forest the lowest-weight edge that will not form a cycle. The key steps of the algorithm are sorting and the use of a disjoint-set data structure to detect cycles.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage names sorting and a disjoint-set data structure for cycle detection as the key steps of Kruskal's algorithm.

claims.text: Kruskal's algorithm runs in O(|E| + |V| log |V|) when a Fibonacci heap is used.

evidence.text: Using a more sophisticated Fibonacci heap, this can be brought down to O(|E| + |V| log |V|), which is asymptotically faster when the graph is dense enough that |E| is ω(|V|), and linear time when |E| is at least |V| log |V|.
evidence.notes: Quoted from the Time complexity section; this bound is stated for Prim's algorithm.

evidence.text: For a graph with E edges and V vertices, Kruskal's algorithm can be shown to run in time O(E log E) time, with simple data structures.

claims.verdict_rationale: The Fibonacci-heap bound is attributed to Prim's algorithm, while the Kruskal passage gives O(E log E); together they refute assigning O(|E| + |V| log |V|) to Kruskal.

claims.text: Prim's algorithm requires all of the graph's edges to be sorted by weight before it begins.

evidence.text: A first improved version uses a heap to store all edges of the input graph, ordered by their weight. This leads to an O(|E| log |E|) worst-case running time. But storing vertices instead of edges can improve it still further.
evidence.notes: Quoted from the Time complexity section.
